🤫 OpenAI 'Quietly' Rolls Out GPT-5.5; Announcement So Stealthy It Trended Worldwide In Minutes

SAN FRANCISCO — whispered, then screamed

MODELS — OpenAI quietly rolled out GPT-5.5 this week — "quietly" being the industry term for a launch with no keynote, just a single vague tweet that instantly detonated across every group chat, newsroom, and family dinner on Earth.

"We didn't want to make a big deal of it," the company said, of a model that was on the front page of six countries by lunch. Analysts note that in tech, "a quiet release" now carries roughly the same decibel level as a fire alarm in a library.

🏠 LG's New Home Robot Promises A 'Zero Labor Home'; Couch Nervously Updates Its Résumé

LAS VEGAS — reported from a suspiciously relaxed living room

ROBOTS — At CES, LG unveiled CLOiD, an AI-powered home robot it says will bring humanity closer to a "Zero Labor Home" — a bold vision in which nobody does anything, ever, and the robot quietly resents all of you for it.

"It handles the chores so you can focus on what matters," a rep explained, gesturing toward a man who was, at that exact moment, focusing on nothing at all with tremendous dedication. Sociologists warn the Zero Labor Home is either utopia or the first ten minutes of a documentary about how it all went wrong.

WOW!

💻 Chipmakers Declare 2026 'The Year Of The Laptop'; Laptops Respond By Still Having 4% Battery

LAS VEGAS — reported from beneath a pile of press releases

HARDWARE — The CPU wars have erupted at CES, with Qualcomm's Snapdragon X2 Elite, AMD's Ryzen AI 400 series, and Intel's Core Ultra Series 3 all declaring 2026 "the year of the laptop" — a title the laptop has held, unconvincingly, every single year since 1994.

"It's up to 40% faster," each company said, of a benchmark only they run. Consumers, thrilled, asked whether it would finally survive one whole video call unplugged, and were met with a long, meaningful silence.

🍞 Everything At CES Now Has A.I., Including A Mattress That Judges How You Sleep

LAS VEGAS — filed from a very opinionated toaster

GADGETS — CES 2026 is in full swing, and the theme is unmistakable: every object now has AI, whether it needed it or not — including a mattress that analyzes your sleep and a fridge that has, frankly, some notes about your diet.

"It's smart!" exhibitors cried, of a trash can that now offers feedback. Attendees report the show floor is a glittering vision of the future in which you will be gently criticized by nine appliances before you have even had coffee.

SHINY

👓 New A.I. Glasses Tell You Things On The Go; Mostly Things You Did Not Ask About

LAS VEGAS — reported at eye level

WEARABLES — A fresh wave of AI glasses debuted at CES, promising to feed you information on the go so you never have to reach for your phone — and, as a bonus, whispering unrequested facts about the pigeon you happen to be looking at.

"It's like having a genius in your ear," a demoer said, of an assistant that had just helpfully identified a door as "a door." Early wearers report the future is bright, informative, and utterly impossible to make stop talking.
